# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Le_2025_meropenem"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Le_2025_meropenem"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-025-01495-3> (open access, PMC12064575)
* Supplement (Online Resources 1-5): electronic supplementary material of the article

Le 2025 is a prospective population PK study of IV meropenem in critically ill
children with sepsis or septic shock (cases) and matched children receiving
meropenem without sepsis (controls). Its novelty is the screening of renal
biomarkers, serum creatinine, serum cystatin C and serum neutrophil
gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), as covariates. The final model (Table 2)
is a two-compartment model with:

* body-size scaling: `(WT/70)` on both volumes and `(WT/70)^0.75` on CL and Q;
* serum cystatin C as a linear effect on the central volume,
  `V1 = 9.74 * (WT/70) * (1 + 0.449 * CYSC/0.45)`;
* modified-Schwartz eGFR as a power effect on clearance,
  `CL = 9.72 * (WT/70)^0.75 * (eGFR/140)^0.169`.

# Population

Twenty-seven children (19 cases, 8 controls) contributed 309 meropenem
concentrations (271 from cases) between March 2019 and January 2023 at Rady
Children's Hospital, San Diego (Le 2025 Results, Table 1). Median age was 11.8
years (range 0.6-19.6), median weight 36.3 kg (7.2-98.0), and 67% were male.
Seventy-four percent were Hispanic; 70% Caucasian and 30% other or unknown race.
Eleven children (all cases) received vasopressors; 88% of controls had
appendicitis. All received meropenem 20 mg/kg (maximum 2000 mg) every 8 h as a
30-min infusion. Renal function ranged from acute kidney injury to augmented
renal clearance: modified-Schwartz eGFR median 138.9 (22.9-364.8)
mL/min/1.73 m^2, serum creatinine 0.33 (0.09-2.57) mg/dL, serum cystatin C 451.1
(178.3-1824.1) ng/mL (Online Resource 3).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Le_2025_meropenem")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lvc` (thetaV1) | `log(9.74)` L | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (thetaV2) | `log(4.53)` L | Table 2 |
| `lcl` (thetaCL) | `log(9.72)` L/h | Table 2 |
| `lq` (thetaQ) | `log(1.66)` L/h | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_cl_q` | `fixed(0.75)` | Methods (Pharmacokinetic Modeling); Table 2 footnote |
| `e_wt_vc_vp` | `fixed(1)` | Methods; Table 2 footnote |
| `e_cysc_vc` (thetaV1-SCys) | 0.449 | Table 2 |
| `e_crcl_cl` (thetaCL-eGFR-MS) | 0.169 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl` | 0.487 (variance) | Table 2 row 'etaCL' |
| `etalvc` (shared by V1 and V2) | 0.306 (variance) | Table 2 row 'etaV1, etaV2'; Results 'assumed to be equal' |
| `propSd` | `sqrt(0.133)` = 0.3647 | Table 2 row 'epsilon' |
| V1 equation | `9.74*(WT/70)*(1+0.449*CYSC/0.45)` | Table 2 footnote |
| V2 equation | `4.53*(WT/70)` | Table 2 footnote |
| CL equation | `9.72*(WT/70)^0.75*(CRCL/140)^0.169` | Table 2 footnote |
| Q equation | `1.66*(WT/70)^0.75` | Table 2 footnote |
| eGFR (modified Schwartz) | `0.413 * height (cm) / SCr (mg/dL)` | Online Resource 1 |
| Two-compartment structure, first-order elimination | n/a | Methods; Results |
| Proportional residual error | n/a | Methods (FOCE with ETA-EPS interaction); Figure 1a |

# Typical-value checks against the published post hoc parameters

Online Resource 3 tabulates the empirical Bayes (post hoc) estimates of each PK
parameter per kilogram. The intercompartmental clearance has no random effect,
so its per-kilogram value depends on weight alone,
`Q/WT = (1.66/70) * (70/WT)^0.25`, and the published range must be reproduced
exactly at the cohort's lightest (7.2 kg) and heaviest (98.0 kg) child. The
peripheral volume per kilogram, `V2/WT = 4.53/70`, has no covariate at all, so
its typical value must equal the published median up to the shared random
effect.

```{r typical-checks}
mod <- readModelDb("Le_2025_meropenem")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta

# Closed-form parameters straight from the Table 2 footnote, written out
# independently of the model object so the comparison below can go red.
le_typical <- function(WT, CYSC, CRCL) {
  data.frame(
    WT = WT, CYSC = CYSC, CRCL = CRCL,
    cl_kg = 9.72 * (WT / 70)^0.75 * (CRCL / 140)^0.169 / WT,
    v1_kg = 9.74 * (WT / 70) * (1 + 0.449 * CYSC / 0.45) / WT,
    v2_kg = 4.53 * (WT / 70) / WT,
    q_kg  = 1.66 * (WT / 70)^0.75 / WT
  )
}

# Same quantities from the packaged model, typical values (etas = 0).
ev_typ <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4, time = 0, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central",
  WT = c(7.2, 98.0, 36.3, 42.4),
  CYSC = c(0.4511, 0.4511, 0.4511, 0.8010),
  CRCL = c(138.92, 138.92, 138.92, 140.06)
)
typ_mod <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ,
                           returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, cl_kg = cl / ev_typ$WT[id], v1_kg = vc / ev_typ$WT[id],
                   v2_kg = vp / ev_typ$WT[id], q_kg = q / ev_typ$WT[id])
typ_cf <- le_typical(ev_typ$WT, ev_typ$CYSC, ev_typ$CRCL)

# The packaged model reproduces the printed equations (numerical identity).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(typ_mod$cl_kg / typ_cf$cl_kg - 1)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(typ_mod$v1_kg / typ_cf$v1_kg - 1)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(typ_mod$v2_kg / typ_cf$v2_kg - 1)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(typ_mod$q_kg / typ_cf$q_kg - 1)) < 1e-8
)

# Q/kg at the weight extremes reproduces Online Resource 3's range 0.022-0.042
# L/h/kg to the printed precision, and at the median weight its median 0.028.
q_range <- round(typ_mod$q_kg[1:3], 3)
stopifnot(
  isTRUE(all.equal(q_range[2], 0.022)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(q_range[1], 0.042)),
  isTRUE(all.equal(q_range[3], 0.028))
)

typ_cf |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    subject = c("Lightest child (7.2 kg)", "Heaviest child (98 kg)",
                "Median covariates (all)", "Median covariates (controls)"),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_kg"), \(x) signif(x, 3))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(subject, WT, CYSC, CRCL, cl_kg, v1_kg, v2_kg, q_kg) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Subject" = subject, "WT (kg)" = WT, "CYSC (mg/L)" = CYSC,
    "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = CRCL, "CL (L/h/kg)" = cl_kg,
    "V1 (L/kg)" = v1_kg, "V2 (L/kg)" = v2_kg, "Q (L/h/kg)" = q_kg
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value parameters per kilogram from the packaged model.")
```

At the median covariates the typical values are CL 0.163 L/h/kg, V1 0.202 L/kg,
V2 0.065 L/kg and Q 0.028 L/h/kg, against published post hoc medians of 0.15,
0.23, 0.06 and 0.028 (Online Resource 3, all participants). The post hoc medians
of 27 children carry the random effects, so agreement within the IIV (CV about
80% on CL and 60% on the volumes) is what is expected; the Q identity is exact.

# Virtual cohort

Individual data are not public. The virtual cohort below draws weight, serum
cystatin C and eGFR independently from log-normal distributions centred on the
published medians, with spreads chosen so the 27-child published ranges sit near
the 2nd and 98th percentiles, truncated to the observed ranges. Covariates are
held constant over the three simulated days (the paper used time-varying values).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2025)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
n_sub <- 200L

rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, median, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- log(hi / lo) / 4
  x <- numeric(0)
  while (length(x) < n) {
    y <- stats::rlnorm(2L * n, log(median), sdlog)
    x <- c(x, y[y >= lo & y <= hi])
  }
  x[seq_len(n)]
}

subj <- tibble::tibble(
  id   = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT   = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 36.3, 7.2, 98.0),
  CYSC = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 0.4511, 0.1783, 1.8241),  # ng/mL / 1000
  CRCL = rtrunc_lnorm(n_sub, 138.92, 22.85, 364.82),
  treatment = "20 mg/kg q8h"
)

# 20 mg/kg (max 2000 mg) every 8 h as 30-min infusions for 3 days (9 doses).
dose_times <- seq(0, 64, by = 8)
doses <- subj |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = dose_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central", amt = pmin(20 * WT, 2000),
                rate = amt / 0.5)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 8, by = 0.1), seq(24, 32, by = 0.25),
                           seq(48, 56, by = 0.1))))
obs <- subj |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = 0, rate = 0)
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$Cc))
```

## Concentration-time profiles on study days 1 and 3

The paper's Online Resource 5 shows the individual observed concentrations; the
sampling design was pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 h after the start of the first
studied infusion and again on days 2 and 3. The panels below show the simulated
5th-95th percentile band and median for the first and the seventh (day 3) dose.

```{r vpc}
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 8 | (time >= 48 & time <= 56)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = ifelse(time <= 8, "Day 1 (first dose)", "Day 3 (seventh dose)"),
    tad = ifelse(time <= 8, time, time - 48)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(day, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~day) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after start of infusion (h)", y = "Meropenem (mg/L)",
       title = "Simulated meropenem concentrations, 20 mg/kg q8h",
       caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 virtual children; compare Online Resource 5 of Le 2025.")
```

## Individual-parameter distribution against Online Resource 3

```{r param-dist}
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, WT, cl, vc, vp, q) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl_kg = cl / WT, v1_kg = vc / WT, v2_kg = vp / WT,
                q_kg = q / WT, ke = cl / vc, thalf = log(2) / ke)

published_or3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~parameter,          ~pub_median, ~pub_min, ~pub_max,
  "CL (L/h/kg)",        0.15,        0.05,     0.49,
  "V1 (L/kg)",          0.23,        0.07,     0.57,
  "V2 (L/kg)",          0.06,        0.03,     0.14,
  "Q (L/h/kg)",         0.028,       0.022,    0.042,
  "ke (1/h)",           0.66,        0.20,     2.33,
  "t1/2 = 0.693/ke (h)", 1.05,       0.30,     3.48
)
sim_or3 <- tibble::tibble(
  parameter = published_or3$parameter,
  sim_median = c(median(indiv$cl_kg), median(indiv$v1_kg), median(indiv$v2_kg),
                 median(indiv$q_kg), median(indiv$ke), median(indiv$thalf)),
  sim_p05 = c(quantile(indiv$cl_kg, 0.05), quantile(indiv$v1_kg, 0.05),
              quantile(indiv$v2_kg, 0.05), quantile(indiv$q_kg, 0.05),
              quantile(indiv$ke, 0.05), quantile(indiv$thalf, 0.05)),
  sim_p95 = c(quantile(indiv$cl_kg, 0.95), quantile(indiv$v1_kg, 0.95),
              quantile(indiv$v2_kg, 0.95), quantile(indiv$q_kg, 0.95),
              quantile(indiv$ke, 0.95), quantile(indiv$thalf, 0.95))
)
or3 <- dplyr::left_join(published_or3, sim_or3, by = "parameter") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = sim_median / pub_median)

# Centre check: a mis-transcribed theta or covariate normaliser (for example
# reading the cystatin C normaliser in ng/mL) moves these medians several-fold.
# The published medians are post hoc estimates from only 27 children (log-scale
# sampling SE of a median about 0.17 for a log-SD of 0.7), and the ratios
# realised here were 0.92-1.16, so the bound is a factor of 1.6.
stopifnot(all(abs(log(or3$ratio)) < log(1.6)))

or3 |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(sim_median, sim_p05, sim_p95, ratio), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Published median" = pub_median,
    "Published min" = pub_min, "Published max" = pub_max,
    "Simulated median" = sim_median, "Simulated P5" = sim_p05,
    "Simulated P95" = sim_p95, "Simulated / published median" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Individual PK parameters: Online Resource 3 post hoc estimates (27 children) vs the 200-child virtual cohort.")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper does not report non-compartmental parameters, so there is no
published NCA table to compare against. PKNCA is used instead to check the
steady-state mass balance over the day-3 dosing interval (48-56 h): at steady
state, `AUC_tau = dose / CL` for every child, an identity that uses each
subject's own simulated clearance.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 48, time <= 56) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_nca <- doses |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 48) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment) |>
  as.data.frame()

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 48, end = 56, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals,
                                          options = list(auc.method = "lin up/log down")))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dose_nca |> dplyr::select(id, amt), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv |> dplyr::select(id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_ratio = auclast / (amt / cl))

# Same drawn parameters on both sides: the residual is trapezoid error on the
# 0.1-h grid plus any approach to steady state still incomplete after six
# doses in the slowest-clearing children.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(nca_wide$auc_ratio) - 1) < 0.02,
  quantile(abs(nca_wide$auc_ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.05
)

nca_wide |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(c(cmax, cmin, auclast, auc_ratio),
                  list(median = median, p05 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.05),
                       p95 = \(x) quantile(x, 0.95)))
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(),
                      names_to = c("parameter", "stat"),
                      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(median|p05|p95)$") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    parameter = dplyr::recode(parameter,
      cmax = "Cmax (mg/L)", cmin = "Cmin (mg/L)",
      auclast = "AUC0-8,ss (mg*h/L)", auc_ratio = "AUC0-8,ss / (dose/CL)"),
    dplyr::across(c(median, p05, p95), \(x) signif(x, 3))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("NCA parameter" = parameter, "Median" = median,
                "P5" = p05, "P95" = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA over the day-3 dosing interval (48-56 h), 20 mg/kg q8h.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Cystatin C units.** Table 2 states that SCys is in ng/mL, but the V1
  equation divides SCys by 0.45. Read literally in ng/mL the ratio would be
  about 1000 at the cohort median (451 ng/mL) and V1 would be several hundred
  times too large. The normaliser 0.45 equals the cohort median expressed in
  mg/L (0.451 mg/L), so the model uses the canonical `CYSC` column in mg/L
  (`CYSC = SCys [ng/mL] / 1000`). The typical V1 per kilogram at the median
  covariates (0.20 L/kg) then agrees with the published post hoc median of
  0.23 L/kg. Note that the study's research ELISA reads lower than the clinical
  immunoturbidimetric assays behind the adult reference range of about
  0.6-1.1 mg/L, so cystatin C values from a clinical assay should not be
  plugged in without considering the assay difference.
- **Variance scale of the random effects.** Table 2 does not say whether the
  eta and epsilon rows are variances or standard deviations. They are taken as
  the raw NONMEM variances. The bootstrap 95% CI relative width of the
  'etaV1, etaV2' row, (0.464 - 0.153)/0.287 = 1.08, matches the width expected
  for a variance estimated from 27 subjects, 3.92 * sqrt(2/27) = 1.07, and is
  twice the width expected for a standard deviation (0.53). The etaCL row (0.83)
  also sits nearer the variance prediction. The residual row is read on the
  same scale (proportional SD `sqrt(0.133) = 36.5%`).
- **Shared random effect on V1 and V2.** Results state that the inter-subject
  variability of V1 and V2 "was assumed to be equal", and Table 2 reports a
  single row 'etaV1, etaV2'. The model uses one eta for both volumes rather
  than two independent etas with equal variance; Online Resource 3 reports
  identical quartile-wise case-versus-control p-values for V1 and V2
  (0.011, <0.001, 0.73, 0.057), which a shared eta produces and two
  independent etas would not.
- **Proportional residual error.** The paper says proportional and additive
  error models were explored but not which was retained. A single epsilon is
  reported, estimation used FOCE with ETA-EPS interaction (which matters only
  for a prediction-dependent error), and the Figure 1a observed-versus-IPRED
  scatter widens with concentration, so a proportional error is used.
- **Cases versus controls.** The final model has no sepsis covariate. Online
  Resource 3 shows lower post hoc CL in cases than controls (0.14 vs 0.29
  L/h/kg) with near-identical median eGFR (138.9 vs 140.1), so that difference
  sits in the random effects and the model's covariates do not reproduce it.
  Part of the V1 difference (0.19 vs 0.29 L/kg) is carried by cystatin C:
  the typical V1 at the control median cystatin C (0.80 mg/L) and weight is
  0.25 L/kg against 0.20 L/kg at the case median (0.43 mg/L).
- **eGFR equation for young adults.** The two participants aged 18 years or
  older had eGFR computed by CKD-EPI rather than the modified Schwartz equation
  (Online Resource 1); the model uses whatever value is supplied in `CRCL`.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight, cystatin C and eGFR are drawn independently
  (the paper reports no correlations), truncated to the published ranges, and
  held constant in time; the paper used time-varying biomarker values with
  nearest-value carry-forward/backward.
- No erratum or correction notice for the article was found (checked
  2026-11-04).
